title: 10 Countries Team Up to Build a Giant Invisible Shield Over Europe!
summary: Imagine a missile flying so fast it could cross a whole country in minutes. That's what Europe is worried about. On Monday, Ukraine and nine other countries announced they are forming a new team to build a giant invisible shield over Europe to stop ballistic missiles—the super-fast, hard-to-catch kind. The countries are Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and Ukraine. They met in Paris with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. They said Ukraine has unique experience because it has been fighting off Russia's missile attacks for over four years. Russia has fired thousands of missiles at Ukraine, hitting cities and knocking out power. The group wants to use that hard-won knowledge to protect the whole continent. The plan is to create an integrated missile defense architecture—basically a network of radars and interceptors that can spot and smash incoming missiles before they hit. They didn't say when it will be ready, and other countries can join later. Russian President Vladimir Putin was not happy. He promised that if Ukraine strikes inside Russia, Russia will hit back even harder. A Kremlin spokesman called the group a 'coalition of warmongers.' Meanwhile, Ukraine is also getting help from the U.S. President Trump said Ukraine can make American Patriot air defense systems, which are really good at shooting down missiles. But experts say that could take years. Ukraine has also been using its own clever drones to strike Russian supply ships. In just one week, they hit 105 Russian vessels near Crimea, causing a big fuel shortage there. The Paris meeting was a big show of support for Ukraine and a warning to Russia that Europe is serious about defense.
why_it_matters: This plan shows that when countries work together, they can build something to protect people from danger—just like safety drills and rules help keep your school safe.

questions.question: What is the 'giant invisible shield' meant to stop?
Which country has been fighting off missile attacks for over four years?
What did a Kremlin spokesman call the new group of countries?
How many Russian vessels did Ukrainian drones hit in one week near Crimea?
What will the network of radars and interceptors do?
Who said Ukraine can make American Patriot air defense systems?

background_read: Ukraine has been defending itself against Russian missile attacks since the war began in 2022. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (the leader of Ukraine since 2019) is now helping other countries learn from that experience.
Russian President Vladimir Putin (who has led Russia for more than 20 years) reacted angrily to the new plan, showing how tense the relationship between Russia and Western Europe has become.
Many countries already use parts of missile defense systems, but a joint European shield would be a big step toward protecting the whole continent together.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ukraine and nine other European countries (Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom)
WHAT: Announced a plan to build an integrated missile defense network (radars and interceptors) over Europe
WHERE: They met in Paris, France
WHY: To stop ballistic missiles and protect the continent, using Ukraine's real-world experience after four years of Russian missile attacks

perspectives.description: The ten countries believe pooling knowledge and technology will make all of Europe safer from fast-moving missiles, and they see Ukraine's hard-won experience as a valuable lesson.
Russian officials call the group a 'coalition of warmongers' and promise to strike back harder if Ukraine hits targets inside Russia, viewing the shield as a threat to their power.
Some experts point out that building such a system takes many years and lots of money, and it may not be able to stop every missile, especially if other countries develop even faster weapons.
